snapshot_markdown:
**AIC Mines (ASX: A1M)** — Gold/Copper Mining, Subiaco, AU. 56 employees. Operates Eloise copper mine (Queensland) and is developing the adjacent Jericho copper deposit. Two segments: mining + exploration/corporate.

### Situational read
Small-cap copper play in active expansion mode. Profitable on TTM basis ($54.7M EBITDA, 50% gross margin) but pouring cash into Eloise plant expansion and Jericho mine development — capex burn of -$86.3M TTM against only $31.9M financing inflow. Stock up 158% YoY on copper thesis. **Mixed operational signals over last 6 months:** Oct 2025 Jefferies note flagged production miss. Dec 2025 quarter copper production was lower (shares dropped). Jan 2026 the company hit cost/production guidance but stock still down. Feb 2026 underground deposit milestone hit but shares fell. Then Mar/Apr 2026 — bounced back with higher Q3 production, asset swap with Cooper Metals, and resource estimate upgrade. Volatile execution.

### Financials (USD, TTM ending Dec 31, 2025)
- Market Cap **$347.6M** (+158% YoY), Enterprise Value **$315.4M** (+187% YoY)
- Total Revenue **$133.8M** (+8% YoY), Gross Margin **50.3%**, EBITDA **$54.7M** (+38% YoY)
- EV/EBITDA 5.77x — cheap relative to peers if execution holds
- Total Assets **$283.5M**, Total Debt **$11.3M**, Total Equity **$214.2M**, D/E 0.05 — almost no leverage
- Capex **-$86.3M TTM** vs financing **+$31.9M** — burning cash on the build, will need to raise again

### Capital structure
$109.4M raised to date, all equity-funded. Recent: **$35.7M PIPE June 2025** led by Hawke's Point (PE) for Eloise expansion + Jericho development. Prior: $37.7M PIPE May 2024 (Jericho drives + ventilation), $21.0M PIPE Feb 2023. PE-friendly cap table: Hawke's Point and FIDES Capital both hold minority positions. No bank debt syndicate. 56 employees executing a multi-project ramp on a thin capital base.

### Recent activity (last 6 months)
Production inconsistency is the dominant theme. Jefferies flagged miss in Oct, Dec quarter production dropped, Jan results showed guidance hit but the market wasn't impressed. Recovery in Q3 2026: higher production, resource estimate upgrade, exploration expansion at North Queensland, and an asset swap with Cooper Metals (Apr 2026). Underlying message: small team executing across too many projects (Jericho, Eloise, Cannington, Windsor, Pyramid, Delamerian, Marymia, Peake/Denison) for a 56-person headcount.

### Top contacts for outreach
1. **Aaron Colleran** — CEO/MD — aaron.colleran@aicmines.com.au
2. **Tim Benfield** — COO — tim.benfield@aicmines.com.au (operational owner — pitch the production volatility angle here)

Main line: +61 (0)2 8259 7000

### Why they'd buy
High fit. Small team (56 people) running 8+ project sites, with documented production volatility flagged by sell-side analysts. Capex-heavy ramp on Jericho + Eloise with PE investor (Hawke's Point) on the cap table — PE owners want operational discipline. Recent earnings calls and quarterly updates show the market is punishing every miss. Operational consulting that smooths quarter-to-quarter delivery is the exact pitch. COO Tim Benfield is the buyer.
